content:
OpenAI has issued its latest statement regarding Apple's lawsuit accusing it of stealing trade secrets. Details below.

OpenAI claims it is "not aware" of any evidence supporting Apple's allegations

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's positioning in the consumer device space.

Shortly after Apple filed the lawsuit, OpenAI's Head of Strategic Communications, Drew Pusateri, responded on behalf of the company on X.

In his post, he claimed that OpenAI "has no interest in the trade secrets of other companies" and added that OpenAI will continue to "focus on developing innovative technologies that empower users around the world."

According to a Bloomberg report, OpenAI has now issued its latest statement regarding the lawsuit:

9to5Mac's perspective

While OpenAI's statement directly denies Apple's allegations, it appears to simultaneously sidestep the substantive content of the complaint.

Apple is not arguing that former employees should not work for competitors—which is generally not permissible under California law—but rather accusing these employees of taking proprietary files, hardware information, and other confidential materials with them when they left.

OpenAI has yet to provide a detailed account of the incident or disclose whether any internal measures have been taken. The only specific public statement so far comes from Apple, whose complaint contains specific allegations, case details, and supporting documentation.

OpenAI is expected to file response documents in the coming days, making its first detailed legal defence against Apple's allegations.
